title: Over-Cap Refund Amount on Member Cost Sharing
content:
The over-cap refund on a Medicaid Managed Care Membership is worked out from three defined quantities: the counting window, the counted total and the member's cap.

## Definitions

**1. Counting window.** The counting window is the number of months in the category's cap period counted back from the review date, a date counting when it lies fewer than that many whole months before the review date. The review date is the date the refund is worked out. Cost sharing dated outside the counting window never counts toward the cap.

**2. Counted total.** The counted total is the member copays on medical claims whose service date falls in the counting window, net of any adjustment entries against those claims, plus the over-cap refunds already booked in the counting window and the pharmacy copays on fills and fill reversals dated in the counting window. Each entry is taken at the amount the ledger shows it: an adjustment entry, an over-cap refund or a fill reversal is carried as a negative amount, so it lowers the counted total. Medical copays and their adjustment entries are placed by service date, over-cap refunds by booked date, and pharmacy copays by fill date.

**3. Member's cap.** The member's cap is the monthly household income on file multiplied by the category's cap-period months, multiplied by the category's cap percent, divided by one hundred and rounded half up to the cent.

**4. Over-cap refund.** The over-cap refund is the counted total less the cap, never below zero, rounded half up to the cent.

**Rounding.** Every rounding to the cent in this calculation is half up: before rounding, a tolerance of 0.0001 cent is added to the amount, so an amount that sits exactly on a half cent is always rounded upward (a cap figure of 185.175 becomes 185.18).

## The same rule, input by input

| Input | Record it is read from | How it is placed in time |
|---|---|---|
| Medical copays and their adjustment entries | The membership's claim ledger | Service date in the counting window |
| Over-cap refunds already booked | The membership's claim ledger | Booked date in the counting window |
| Pharmacy copays on fills and fill reversals | The member's pharmacy fill history | Fill date in the counting window |
| Monthly household income | The membership, as on file | On file at the review date |
| Cap-period months and cap percent | The member's eligibility category | The category's figures |

## Worked figure (hypothetical inputs)

The following inputs are invented for illustration and are not company figures or any member's record: a category cap period of 3 months, a category cap percent of 5.00, a monthly household income on file of 2,150.00 USD.

- Medical copays with service dates in the window total 310.00; one adjustment entry against one of those claims is carried at negative 6.00, so the net medical copays are 304.00.
- No over-cap refund has been booked in the window.
- Pharmacy copays dated in the window total 24.40, and one fill reversal is carried at negative 3.40, so the pharmacy copays count as 21.00.
- Counted total: 304.00 plus 21.00, which is 325.00.
- Cap: 2,150.00 multiplied by 3, multiplied by 5.00, divided by one hundred, which is 322.50.
- Over-cap refund: 325.00 less 322.50, which is 2.50.

With the same cap and a counted total of 318.00, the counted total less the cap would be below zero, so the over-cap refund is 0.00.

## Points of judgement

- **Does a copay on a claim serviced before the window count because it was booked inside it?** No. A medical copay is placed by its service date; a service date outside the window keeps it out of the counted total.
- **Is the cap rounded before it is compared?** Yes. The cap is rounded half up to the cent as a figure in its own right, and the refund is then rounded half up to the cent again.
